data.name: forking

data.name: problem
data.source: searchParams — the reason a rejected forkStrategy redirected back with. Two producers: a platform `refused`, and — since `the-outcome-reaches-the-person` — the action's own pre-perform re-read failing or the strategy having left the roster, both prefixed 'Nothing was attempted: …'

data.name: name
data.source: searchParams — the typed name, round-tripped so a refusal does not also discard what was typed. It now travels on the two 'Nothing was attempted' bounces as well, not only on a platform refusal

components.purpose: Offer a private, editable copy of a platform-owned strategy the user cannot edit — a ceremony page that carries one optional input, the copy's name.
components.current_implementation: max-w-2xl centered column, space-y-4, p-6. Four post-connection branches, and since `the-outcome-reaches-the-person` all four mount `<CarriedProblem>` unconditionally as the first thing under the h1; it renders null when nothing rode in, so each `-with-problem` pairing above is a real rendering rather than a per-branch decision. Deliberately NO confirmation token: forking creates something new and changes nothing that exists, so there is no blast radius to name — a confirmation here would train users to click through the ones that matter (DL-105). The form state carries two plain text-sm paragraphs: the original belongs to BattleGrid and cannot be edited, the copy is yours and starts identical to revision N; nothing about the original changes and the copy has no agents until one is bound. DT-0021 restyled exactly one sentence here — `unreadable`'s: the roster read's reason is now `rounded-gc-2 border border-danger-default bg-danger-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary` with role=alert, with WhyNotLoaded's reassurance following as a separate plain `mt-2` paragraph beneath the block rather than inside it, and the way out is the roster. The at-capacity explanation was deliberately left plain and still is: a bare `role=status text-sm` paragraph, because being full is a standing fact about the account rather than a failed attempt. `no-such-strategy` carries no reason paragraph at all. Note `at-capacity-with-problem`: a role=alert danger banner above that untinted role=status explanation — a bounced attempt above a standing fact, and the difference in weight is the point. A second hidden input now carries sourceRevision — the revision the prose above names — so the copy is taken from what the page showed rather than from the perform's re-read.
constraints: Every branch renders the carried reason, not just the one that can offer a form — the branch that drops it loses the only record of what the click did, and `tests/agent/refusals-reach-the-operator.test.ts` asserts one `<CarriedProblem>` per `<main>` on this page. A design that suppresses it on a terminal branch changes behavior and is requires-spec-change.
No confirmation ceremony may be added — DL-105's ruling, stated in the page: a consequence-free confirmation erodes the ones that carry consequence. Adding one is behavior and requires-spec-change.

The unreadable reason keeps role=alert and the danger treatment DT-0021 landed; the at-capacity explanation was deliberately left out of that sweep and must stay out of it — capacity is a fact about the account, not a failure, and tinting it as one reverses a decided ruling.
WhyNotLoaded's reassurance must survive verbatim wherever it renders relative to the danger block — the tint says something failed; only those words say what did not.
The page renders whole from one server round trip — no client JS, no hydration. A design requiring client-side interactivity changes behavior and is requires-spec-change.

The copy is offered instead of editing, never alongside it — openspec/specs/strategy-authoring/spec.md:206-209 ('they are offered a private copy to change instead … the original is not presented as editable').

components.purpose: Show BattleGrid's answer to a fork it declined — or the news that nothing was attempted — whole and unglossed, on the form acted from.
components.current_implementation: The shared `CarriedProblem` component (src/presentation/components/carried-problem.tsx), extracted by `the-outcome-reaches-the-person` from the copy that used to be inline on this page. DT-0004's danger treatment unchanged — rounded-gc-2 border border-danger-default bg-danger-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary with role=alert and a semibold 'Refused: ' prefix — and it returns null for a falsy `problem`, which is what lets all four branches mount it unconditionally. Its prop now takes `string | null | undefined` (widened by `a-lost-authority-is-not-a-refusal` so a caller reading a parsed query, which yields null, is not tempted to hand-roll a copy); rendering is unchanged. On the unreadable branch it now sits above a block wearing the identical treatment, since DT-0021 gave that page's own reason the danger role too. The page adds no diagnosis the platform did not state.
constraints: role=alert must survive.

The reason reaches the user in the platform's own words, whatever its code — spec.md:230-234 ('the reason is shown in the platform's words, on the form acted from … no cause the platform did not state is offered'). Name collisions surface upstream as a bare INTERNAL_ERROR, so the wording here must survive an unhelpful platform answer without the page glossing it. The action's own 'Nothing was attempted: …' sentences ride the same field and take the same treatment.
This banner appears above a still-usable form with the typed name preserved — a design must keep both facts visible together.
Shared by six ceremony pages (agent deploy/undeploy/rebind, strategy archive/restore/fork) — restyle it in the component, never per page.

components.purpose: Refuse the copy before any work is typed, because the account has no room for another strategy.
components.current_implementation: Its own full-page branch: h1 'No room for another strategy', a `<CarriedProblem>` mount beneath the h1 (usually null; a refused fork that also finds the account full renders both), the platform-derived explanation as a bare text-sm paragraph with role=status (advisory, not failure) — left untinted by DT-0021 on purpose while the unreadable reason took danger — and one underlined link back. Reachable by address only — the roster and the strategy page no longer offer a copy control they know cannot work — but it still refuses honestly and still leads somewhere.
constraints: role=status must survive — being at capacity is a fact about the account, not an error.
No fork form may render in this state — spec.md:215-218 ('the control that would make a copy is not offered, and its absence is explained where it would have been').
'Nothing is styled to look disabled when retrying cannot help' (system.json principle) — explain, do not dim.

components.purpose: Reassure someone staring at a failed read that the strategy still exists, by naming the accurate external cause.
components.current_implementation: Shared WhyNotLoaded component (why-not-loaded.tsx), rendered only in the unreadable state — one plain `mt-2` paragraph, a sibling *after* DT-0021's danger block rather than inside it; the component itself was untouched by that ticket.
constraints: The two causes must stay distinguishable — a 401 is not an outage.
The reassurance sentence is the point and must not be cut for space.

components.purpose: Carry the copy decision: the optional name, one committing button, one visible way out.

actions.effect: POSTs the server action with strategyId and the name only when one was typed; success lands on the copy's edit page (/strategies/[newId]/edit), refusal redirects back here with ?problem= and the typed name preserved as ?name=, and a pre-perform re-read that fails or a strategy that has left the roster also redirects back here with ?problem= prefixed 'Nothing was attempted: …' — carrying ?name= too

components.current_implementation: space-y-4 form; one hidden input (strategyId), the name field, then a flex flex-wrap gap-3 button row. Since `the-outcome-reaches-the-person` the action reads its own re-read: an unreadable roster and a strategy no longer in it each bounce back to this route with a 'Nothing was attempted: …' problem and the typed name, where they used to redirect to /strategies unexplained and drop what was typed.
constraints: A click that reached no operation still lands somewhere that says so, with the typed name intact — the two 'Nothing was attempted: …' paths must not be redesigned back into a silent redirect to the roster.
The form must keep exactly one submit path.
Cancel must remain a visible peer of the submit, never a text link beneath it (DT-0002 ruling, restated in control.ts).

A refused copy returns to this form with the typed name intact — spec.md:233 ('the name the user typed is still in the form'); a design must not turn the refusal into a page that starts the user over.

components.purpose: Optionally name the copy, so the user's copies of the same parent can be told apart.

actions.effect: Sets the name POSTed with the fork; blank means no name is sent and the platform names the copy itself

components.current_implementation: LABEL constant ('Name for the copy (optional)') over a text input wearing CONTROL, maxLength=50 — the platform's declared bound on the argument, pre-stated so it is met by construction rather than discovered by refusal. Beneath it a text-sm helper paragraph: left blank, BattleGrid names the copy '<parent> (fork)' — and names every copy the same way — and a name of your own tells your copies apart.
constraints: maxLength 50 is the platform's declared bound — spec.md:220-223 ('the control accepts no more than the platform's declared length bound'); a design must not remove or relax it.

The helper copy claims no more than the truth supports — spec.md:190-194: the product 'SHALL NOT promise that naming avoids any platform behaviour it has not established'. It says a name tells copies apart, never that it avoids an error; that wording boundary must survive a copy rewrite.
The blank-name outcome ('<parent> (fork)') is said before the copy is made — spec.md:225-228 ('the form said which name that would be before they chose').
Styling changes go through the CONTROL and LABEL constants in control.ts — not per-page classNames.

components.purpose: Make the copy. Labelled 'Make my copy'.
components.current_implementation: BUTTON_PRIMARY constant from control.ts — accent.default bg, min-h-control (44px), rounded-gc-2, DT-0004 hover/active. No pending/loading state between click and redirect — same class of gap as #153; behavior, not styling. DT-0022 added the primitive's `disabled` treatment to this constant — bg.sunken ground, text.disabled label, border.subtle edge and cursor not-allowed, stated rather than an opacity. DT-0022 defined the primitive's `disabled` treatment on this constant, but **nothing in the product enters it** — so it is not listed as a state of this surface. system.json declares it and DT-0022 styles it; a surface claiming a state it cannot reach is the same fiction DT-0003 refused for the ghost and danger variants.
constraints: Styling changes go through the BUTTON_PRIMARY constant in control.ts.
44px minimum tap target (system.json principle).
Focus ring comes from the one global rule in globals.css — do not add a per-element ring.

components.purpose: Decline the copy and return to the strategy being copied, not the roster.
components.current_implementation: An anchor wearing BUTTON_SECONDARY — inline-flex centering, min-h-control, DT-0004 hover. Label 'Cancel'.
constraints: Must remain an anchor (pure navigation, no form participation) and must remain a visible peer of the submit.
Styling changes go through the BUTTON_SECONDARY constant in control.ts.
44px minimum tap target (system.json principle).

components.purpose: Turn away a request without authority, with the one remedy that works: connect.
components.current_implementation: Shared NotConnected component (require-connection.tsx): h1 + message, connect link as an anchor wearing BUTTON_SECONDARY (DT-0006). Inherited by every authenticated page.
constraints: Every no-authority cause renders this same page by design (see design W-C) — a design must not invent per-cause variants.

flows.name: Fork with a name
steps: arrive from a platform strategy's page
type a name (bounded to 50)
submit 'Make my copy'
land on the copy's edit page

flows.name: Fork with the name left blank
steps: read that blank means '<parent> (fork)', every time
submit with no name
no name is sent; the platform names the copy
land on the copy's edit page

flows.name: The platform refuses the copy
steps: submit
platform refuses, whatever its code
redirected back here with ?problem= and ?name=
problem banner in the platform's words above the form, typed name still in the field

flows.name: Nothing could be attempted
steps: submit
the action's re-read of the roster fails, or the strategy is no longer in it
redirected back here with ?problem= 'Nothing was attempted: …' and ?name=
whichever branch renders next carries that sentence — including the branch reporting its own fresh read failure

flows.name: Arrive at capacity
steps: open the fork address while the account is full
'No room for another strategy' with the platform-derived explanation
no form is offered; one link back to the strategy

flows.name: Walk away
steps: click 'Cancel'
back on /strategies/[id], nothing changed

accessibility.notes: The carried problem (shared CarriedProblem, mounted on all four branches) and the unreadable reason carry role=alert; the at-capacity explanation carries role=status. Since DT-0021 the two alerts are visually identical as well, so on `unreadable-with-problem` only wording and order tell them apart. Focus ring is global (focus-visible, 2px). No client JS: every state change is a full navigation, so stacked alerts are read in document order rather than as live-region updates.
